newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Thai stocks down on bank restrictions - HK traders.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks down on bank restrictions - HK traders.

text.p: Regional traders in Hong Kong said on Monday a sharp sell-off in Thai stocks was linked to newly restrictive measures launched by the Bank of Thailand.
"These new restrictive measures on banks raising cheap foreign loans, it's going to squeeze margins further," said one regional trader with a U.S. brokerage.

Traders and fund managers in Hong Kong, who move money around the region, denied a stocks sell-off in both Thailand and Manila was linked to a recent trading scandal at Jardine Fleming Investment Management.
Instead, they said local factors caused both Thailand and Manila to buck a generally positive trend around the region.
In Manila, a quiet period following a strong showing over the past few months has persuaded foreign funds to place money elsewhere, said one fund manager.
"They'll be back to the Philippines sooner than they will Thailand," he said.
A Jardine Fleming spokesman said his company was active in the Thailand market following a re-weighting last week.
"What actually happened was we moved Thailand from a neutral to an underweight position and our broking side in Bangkok did create some sale orders from London-based clients," he said.

Newly restrictive foreign loan requirements prompted the re-weighting and persuaded foreigners, who remained neutral to overweight on Thailand until Friday, to sell heavily, particularly in banking and finance stocks.

"Effectively this tightens money supply even further which means a slowing economy will get even slower," said one foreign fund manager. "Everybody's revising corporate earnings, GDP, you name it, downwards."
